name: stripe-cli-drainable-streaming-sessions
instr:
Stripe CLI cannot gracefully drain long-running webhook, log-tail, websocket, and local gRPC sessions. Introduce a shared lifecycle that closes admission, delivers all accepted work to its existing observable destination, and exposes one deterministic terminal outcome. Preserve existing retry, output, error, flag, and protocol-close behavior.

The `streamlifecycle` package exports `Outcome`, `Report`, `ErrDraining`, `Coordinator`, `NewCoordinator`, `Admission`, and their declared methods. Admission tokens independently account for accepted work until completion. Draining is irreversible, waits for admitted work, returns stable reports to concurrent and later requests, and lets a canceled waiter return without concealing eventual completion.

`NewCoordinator() *Coordinator`, `NewClient(url string, websocketID string, websocketAuthorizedFeature string, cfg *Config) *Client`, `Init(ctx context.Context, cfg *Config) (*Proxy, error)`, and `NewTailer(cfg *Config) *Tailer` construct public drainable components.

Websocket shutdown stops application dispatch, finishes active handlers and both pumps, and performs the established close sequence once. Proxy completion covers every accepted endpoint delivery, result, acknowledgement, and websocket response. Recoverable endpoint errors remain results. Report terminal failures only after prior outcomes remain observable. Tailer completion preserves ordered accepted logs and authorization recovery, closing output only after draining.
